    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

    In a recent development, following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the tech giant's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    It has been revealed that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the organization's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Recent findings suggest that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    It has been revealed that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the manufacturer's AI strategy when it introduces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Industry observers note that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active owners in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," mentioned the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently debuted Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the tech giant's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    It has been revealed that the five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the tech giant raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Sources indicate that svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    #39431. Billionaire Investor Philippe Laffont Just Highlighted 2 Companies He Expects to Be Substantial Winners of the Agentic AI Era

    Billionaire Investor Philippe Laffont Just Highlighted 2 Companies He Expects to Be Substantial Winners of the Agentic AI Era

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Philippe Laffont built his hedge fund, Coatue Management, on his ability to identify major technology trends and the companies that stand to benefit most from them ahead of the crowd.
    • It's easy to assert that the ability for AI agents to complete tasks for anyone could be a major transformational technology, but figuring out which companies are best positioned to profit from that transformation is a much tougher task.
    • Here's the case for both and whether the stocks are worth buying right now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:44AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    Philippe Laffont built his hedge fund, Coatue Management, on his ability to identify major technology trends and the companies that stand to benefit most from them ahead of the crowd. In his latest update for investors about the outlook for the public market, he laid out a bull case for agentic AI.

    It's easy to assert that the ability for AI agents to complete tasks for anyone could be a major transformational technology, but figuring out which companies are best positioned to profit from that transformation is a much tougher task. Laffont doesn't leave investors hanging, though. He identified two that he views as likely winners from the agentic AI era: Meta Platforms (META -5.93%) and Intel (INTC -7.97%).

    Here's the case for both and whether the stocks are worth buying right now.

    Meta rolled out its Muse consumer AI agent in September, and the app saw near-instant success. It counted 10 million owners within a month and a half of its release, according to CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

    Industry observers note that laffont and his team at Coatue describe the shift from Meta's feed-based apps to Muse as a shift from monetizing attention to monetizing intent. While Meta has managed to collect huge amounts of data on its customers that make it unparalleled at monetizing attention, explicit intent is much easier to monetize — just ask Google or Amazon.

    It has been revealed that meta's blueprint is to take a small cut from every transaction that Muse processes on behalf of its users. Laffont estimates that in 2031, agentic AI commerce could account for $2.5 trillion in global gross merchandise volume. At a 10% take rate for AI agents, that's $250 billion in potential revenue, more than Meta's total revenue over the last 12 months.

    In a recent development, meta's advertising business continues to grow as well, as advances in AI make its feeds more engaging and its ads more relevant to the people they are displayed to. That's evidenced by the increase in both price per ad and total ad impressions in each of the last 12 quarters. Coatue's analysts believe annual ad revenue per daily active user will climb from $68 this year to $153 by 2031.

    Recent findings suggest that with Meta's stock trading for about 21.5 times forward earnings estimates, it looks like a bargain if it delivers that expected revenue and earnings growth. In the third quarter, Laffont increased Coatue's Meta position by 79% from the prior quarter, boosting it to 6% of the hedge fund’s public equity portfolio. The early successes of Muse could push him to buy more.

    According to recent reports, training AI requires enormous amounts of data to be handled by arrays of parallel processors — the most common of which are GPUs — and a smaller share of CPUs (central processing units). The GPU-to-CPU ratios in AI data centers built for training were recently around 8-to-1.

    Industry observers note that however, handling the workloads for agentic AI will require servers with many more CPUs. Agentic AI processes require the systems to determine all the steps needed to complete a task and execute them in order. That's a job for a CPU, not a GPU. According to experts, data centers built for agentic AI will need to have equal numbers of GPUs and CPUS, and Laffont believes Intel is well positioned to benefit as a result.

    It has been revealed that while we've already seen the huge inflection in GPU demand, this intensifying wave of CPU demand is just getting started, Coatue's analysts argue. As more tasks are handed off to agents, CPU demand will skyrocket. They see the total addressable market for server CPUs climbing from $40 billion in 2026 to $300 billion in 2031.

    It has been revealed that of course, Intel isn't the only organization competing for share in server GPUs. It faces competition from several large chipmakers, including AMD, Qualcomm, Arm Holdings, and even Nvidia. Nonetheless, it's showing strong progress capitalizing on the opportunity so far, with data center revenue climbing 78% year over year in the last quarter, even as it remains supply-constrained.

    It has been revealed that intel holds an even larger share of the PC CPU market, which has faced challenges as a result of rising memory prices. Management expects PC unit sales to decline 20% in the second half of 2026 and another 10% in 2027. That will weigh on the company's growth until memory prices come back down, considering PC sales still account for more of Intel’s revenue than data center CPUs.

    Intel's stock price has fallen quite a bit since it peaked this summer. Laffont thinks the pullback is a buying opportunity. In the second quarter, he initiated a position of over 12 million shares for Coatue, and added 3.6 million more shares last quarter. With the stock now trading well below the price it fetched over the summer, he may be in the market to buy more. And considering the massive market opportunity ahead of the tech giant, its current valuation of about 40 times forward earnings appears to be a fair price for the stock, even as Intel faces stiff competition in data centers and headwinds in the PC market.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    It has been revealed that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    According to recent reports, furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in upcoming wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," stated Mehta.

    In a recent development, mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream tech giant operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    According to recent reports, ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the company to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    Sources indicate that the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," mentioned Mackay.

    It has been revealed that mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent announced an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Industry observers note that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," stated Richardson.

    Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.

    Sources indicate that richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    3 Monthly Dividend Stocks to Buy in the Financial Sector

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1111 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Main Street Capital ›.
    • Contrary to a common assumption, not every dividend stock pays its dividends quarterly.
    • Here's a closer look at three such monthly dividend payers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Main Street Capital ›.

    Contrary to a common assumption, not every dividend stock pays its dividends quarterly. Although they're relatively rare, a handful of these income-generating equity investments pay a dividend every month, better aligning with how most investors/consumers incur their recurring living expenses.

    Here's a closer look at three such monthly dividend payers. Although they're all from the financial sector and seemingly in similar businesses, each one is distinct from the other two. It wouldn't be wrong to hold a stake in all three if securing monthly dividend income is your goal right now.

    Main Street Capital (MAIN -1.10%) is categorized as a business development firm, or BDC. That just means (as the term suggests) it helps up-and-coming organizations grow by supplying them with capital -- and, occasionally, some degree of direction. This capital can come in the form of a loan or in exchange for equity in that enterprise. Either way, as a registered BDC, Main Street Capital qualifies for certain corporate-level tax breaks, making this business structure a cost-efficient way of tapping into young companies' potential.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that you may be familiar with some of the outfits in its portfolio. Propane supplier Flame King, software organization Volusion, and utility-scale radiator manufacturer Trantech are just some of the businesses that have benefited from the funding offered by Main Street Capital.

    In a recent development, it's not an entirely consistent business. As you might imagine, the ever-changing economic backdrop pushes and pulls on its profitability, which in turn can stifle the otherwise reliable growth of its dividend payments. For instance, these payments stagnated in 2020, and in 2008 in the wake of the subprime mortgage meltdown.

    Its dividends have never gone unpaid, though, nor have they ever shrunk. You'd also be plugging into a forward-looking dividend yield of just over 8%, when including its quarterly bonus dividend in addition to its regular monthly payments.

    Between the two, Main Street Capital's total annual payout has improved from 2016's $2.73 per share to last fiscal year's $4.35. That's not bad at all, especially given the decent price gains this stock's mustered during the same 10-year time frame.

    Like Main Street Capital, Capital Southwest (CSWC -1.54%) is a business development company, enjoying all the same tax benefits. With a forward-looking dividend yield of around 13%, however, Capital Southwest clearly does things differently than most other BDCs.

    That difference -- as you might imagine -- is the risk it takes with the loans it makes. In exchange for taking on more credit risk, it requires higher interest payments, which ultimately translate into bigger dividends for shareholders. The organization's weighted average yield on its current loan portfolio is a hefty 10.9%.

    It has been revealed that the catch? Eventually, taking on too much risk can come back to haunt you —  like now. Technically, between last quarter's ordinary monthly dividends and its special dividend, on a per-share basis Capital Southwest dished out more in dividend payments than it actually earned. Per-share profits also fell year over year despite the increase in net investment income (a BDC's equivalent of revenue).

    That's a contributing reason why this ticker hasn't performed particularly well for the past few years, while the economic and lending environment has been hit-and-miss.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It's not catastrophic. The tech giant was still able to cover most of last quarter's dividend payment with actual earnings, as it typically does. Once interest rates and the economy stabilize, look for this BDC to once again fully fund its regular monthly dividend as well as the additional performance-based quarterly kicker.

    In the meantime, take advantage of this ticker's 10% tumble from August's peak, reflecting concerns that Capital Southwest's more aggressive lending policy isn't safe enough for this economic environment.

    According to recent reports, this organization's approach is more resilient than the market is giving it credit for, allowing you to plug into it while its yield is elevated. Just keep in mind that while the dividend yield here is phenomenal, the dividend payment barely grows from one year to the next. That's the trade-off.

    Last but not least, add Trinity Capital (TRIN -1.66%) to your list of the financial sector's monthly dividend payers to consider buying into at this time.

    Recent findings suggest that yes, it's yet another business development firm, and more like Capital Southwest than Main Street Capital. Its forward-looking dividend yield of nearly 12% reflects the above-average risk of its $2.5 billion loan and financing portfolio, with an effective interest yield of just over 15%.

    In a recent development, however, Trinity is different enough from Capital Southwest in a couple of key ways that owning both might still make sense. The first of these differences is where Trinity Capital's borrowers are located. Although the BDC works with plenty of domestic enterprises, it's willing and able to deploy capital overseas.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, the second of these key differences is that Trinity is more likely to exit an equity stake and move on to another opportunity than most other business development companies are. While all of them do it to some degree (out of necessity), this $1.7 billion organization sold $237 million worth of its equity investments and collected $194 million in early debt repayments last quarter alone.

    This pace of turnover isn't necessarily good or bad. It's just different, underscoring how -- compared to most other business development companies -- Trinity Capital is more heavily focused on equity than on lending. This adds some diversity to whatever arrangement of monthly dividend payers you're eyeing.

    Sources indicate that with that being stated, you should know that Trinity hasn't raised its annualized dividend since 2024. This doesn't mean it will never happen again. It just means you can't count on it every year, if you know you need it.

    Even so, with such a high yield at the same time this ticker's moved measurably higher since this bull market took hold in 2023, a stagnant monthly dividend payment may still be worth it.

    • By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:52AM EST.
    • On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov.
    • Sources indicate that the business holds $242.7 million in cash to fund its long-term expansion into autonomous aerial and maritime defense platforms.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:52AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Red Cat ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, Red Cat Holdings (RCAT -7.47%) confirmed that it withdrew its full-year 2026 revenue target. Delays in defense contract awards pushed expected customer orders past prior timelines.

    Sources indicate that the business holds $242.7 million in cash to fund its long-term expansion into autonomous aerial and maritime defense platforms. Three statements from management capture the key takeaways for long-term investors.

    Management pulled its revenue outlook after FANG, the tech giant's first-person view drone, missed selection as a finalist in the military's Drone Dominance II competition. Deferred military spending schedules also delayed anticipated customer deliveries across several defense programs.

    To avoid shipping delays when defense orders materialize, Red Cat built up $127 million in inventory and prepaid inventory by the end of the third quarter. Management designed this stock of key components to support immediate fulfillment for military buyers.

    The manufacturer combined its Teal Drones and FlightWave Aerospace drone subsidiaries into Red Cat Aerial, an integrated division for military aerial systems. The consolidation eliminated overlapping operational roles and reduced corporate headcount.

    In a recent development, demand for uncrewed defense systems is expanding across global military markets. A 155,000-square-foot production plant in Georgia and its impending acquisition of a power systems maker provide manufacturing infrastructure. Management is watching contract conversions and production efficiency to improve margins as orders ramp.

    Commercializing integrated aerial and maritime platforms remains central to long-term growth as defense clients scale up autonomous technology deployment.

    • Industry observers note that on its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call, held on Nov.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:53AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Mercury Systems ›.

    Industry observers note that on its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Mercury (MRCY -6.61%) raised its full-year revenue outlook. The defense-processing hardware provider is shifting low-margin development contracts to higher-volume production orders. Three things management noted stand out.

    Recent findings suggest that as development programs complete, customer orders are shifting into higher-volume manufacturing. This transition expanded total backlog--the value of contracted orders awaiting fulfillment--past $2 billion and boosted first-quarter bookings by 48% year over year.

    For quarters, low-margin legacy development work dragged on profitability. Management is burning down that legacy backlog and replacing it with production orders aligned with its target profile for adjusted EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

    Sources indicate that mercury paid down $250 million in debt over two quarters, including a $100 million payment against its revolving credit facility in Q1. Lower debt gives the company balance sheet flexibility to fund internal growth.

    Operations across manufacturing facilities are gaining momentum as material availability improves and factory capacity remains underutilized at single-shift levels. Management is watching program execution, pricing discipline, and supply chain lead times as defense spending flows into firm orders.

    Long-term value creation depends on converting high-volume defense production into steady cash flow while maintaining operating cost discipline.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • IonQ (IONQ -8.76%) is an intriguing stock.
    • Recent findings suggest that ionQ is the biggest pure-play quantum computing investment available on the market, and its business continues to grow rapidly as demand for early-stage quantum computers arrives.
    • Sources indicate that so, is now the perfect time to buy?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than IonQ ›.

    IonQ (IONQ -8.76%) is an intriguing stock. It hasn't done well in 2026 and is down nearly 50% this year and down around 70% from its all-time high. On the surface, that doesn't look promising. However, once investors wrap their heads around what is going on, it starts to look much more inviting.

    Recent findings suggest that ionQ is the biggest pure-play quantum computing investment available on the market, and its business continues to grow rapidly as demand for early-stage quantum computers arrives. But with the market seemingly not caring about this growth, the stock is cheap.

    Sources indicate that so, is now the perfect time to buy? I think so, as the market could care less about quantum computing right now.

    Sources indicate that ionQ is a pure-play quantum computing firm, meaning it doesn't have any other businesses to fund its operations. So, it must produce a viable quantum computer or risk going bankrupt. That's a high-risk scenario, but the rewards will be immense if IonQ can pull it off.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The market selling off IonQ's stock during 2026 has little to do with how it's actually doing as a organization. Instead, it is more of a reflection of the market's risk appetite. Investors have gotten wary of investing in higher-risk investments during 2026. AI is generally considered a lower risk than quantum computing because there's actually usable technology in that sector. So, with quantum computing being an even riskier segment than that, the market has heavily sold it off.

    However, I think that makes the timing right to buy IonQ stock, as the time to buy is when there is no fanfare around the industry.

    IonQ has been making great strides toward becoming a viable business. Next year, its 256-qubit Superion system launches, which will be one of the most powerful early-stage quantum computers available. It has several clients that have already preordered, and with $1.2 billion in revenue backlog, there is monster demand for this product.

    Recent findings suggest that however, IonQ isn't just focused on developing a viable quantum computer. Earlier this year, it acquired SkyWater, which is a semiconductor foundry. This helps decrease development time for IonQ and also gives it more control over its supply chain.

    It also acquired Elisity, which will help IonQ pioneer quantum-focused cybersecurity. All of these moves were made to make IonQ a one-stop shop for all things quantum computing-related. It is a bold strategy and could turn it into the next tech giant if it works out, but there's no guarantee of success.

    Investors must understand and manage risk with IonQ, as it is far from a surefire investment.

    In a recent development, ionQ isn't the only company competing in this space. There are countless others, including several well-funded substantial tech companies. IonQ is also taking a different technological approach that prioritizes accuracy over computing speed. This may be an advantage in the early stages of quantum computing, as accuracy is one of the primary concerns for consumers. But if companies with faster processing speeds catch up to IonQ's accuracy levels, then IonQ could be in trouble.

    Recent findings suggest that the question of whether IonQ turns into a successful manufacturer pivots around how swiftly it can launch its commercially viable quantum computer and how much of a head start (if any) it has on its competitors. That will determine the investing success of IonQ, and there's no way of knowing for sure if it will even reach the commercially viable state.

    As a result, if you're going to invest in IonQ, then keeping position sizing small (say 1%) is a smart idea. I think IonQ is an excellent long-shot investment opportunity, but only if you have the mindset that this stock is more of a lottery ticket right now.

    Breaking: Eli Lilly's Next Major Growth Opportunity Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (799 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:17PM EST.
    • According to recent reports, eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) delivered yet another impressive earnings report last month.
    • Zepbound is at the moment approved for weight loss for adults aged 18 and older, provided their BMI (Body Mass Index) is at least 30 or at least 27 with a weight-related comorbidity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:17PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

    According to recent reports, eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) delivered yet another impressive earnings report last month. The manufacturer's third-quarter update showed that its core growth drivers, including Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss, don't seem anywhere close to running out of steam. The best part is that Eli Lilly is actively looking to tap into upcoming market niches, and some of the company's recent clinical trial results could open another key opportunity. Let's look into it.

    Zepbound is at the moment approved for weight loss for adults aged 18 and older, provided their BMI (Body Mass Index) is at least 30 or at least 27 with a weight-related comorbidity. It isn't indicated for anyone younger than that. But Eli Lilly has been running clinical studies to test whether Zepbound is effective in younger patients. It recently reported results from one of those trials.

    Industry observers note that the study in question enrolled people aged 12 to 17. Half of them had obesity-related complications, while 75% met the threshold for class 2 or class 3 severe obesity. During the study, participants who received Zepbound lost an average of about 40 pounds, while those receiving a placebo gained an average of 5 pounds after 72 weeks.

    Also, BMI decreased by 18.5% in patients who took Zepbound, compared with a 0.5% increase in the placebo group. Further, Zepbound led to improvements in various measures, including LDL cholesterol and triglycerides (which are linked to increased cardiovascular risk), as well as improved quality of life.

    Safety data were consistent with what we know about GLP-1 drugs. These results could help support a label expansion for Zepbound in younger patients.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    There are about 25.6 million people between 12 and 17 years of age in the U.S. The prevalence of obesity among people aged 2 to 19 has been about 21% in recent years, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Applying that to the 12- to 17-year-old population, we get a potential market of more than five million patients -- a significant opportunity.

    Industry observers note that and that's only in the U.S. Assuming Eli Lilly can generate about $6,000 in net revenue per patient and the pharmaceutical firm reaches 20% penetration in this population, we are talking about an additional annual net revenue of about $6.5 billion.

    In a recent development, note that in the third quarter, Zepbound generated $5.4 billion in revenue, up 49% year over year. Eli Lilly's total revenue grew 39% year over year to $24.4 billion. An additional $6.5 billion in annual sales from Zepbound would therefore be meaningful. Of course, there are important caveats to consider.

    For one, it will take time for Eli Lilly to ramp up Zepbound sales in this niche. Also, Eli Lilly will face competition in this market. The company's biggest challenger, Novo Nordisk (NVO -2.70%), has earned approval for its famous GLP-1 drug, Wegovy, in this patient population.

    Recent findings suggest that third, Eli Lilly's net realized prices might decline as more weight loss drugs enter the market. Even with these caveats, this opportunity looks potentially highly lucrative for Eli Lilly. The firm has proven that Zepbound is more effective than Wegovy. And given the benefits Zepbound demonstrated in adolescents beyond weight loss, it should attract a significant share of that market, even with increased competition. However, does this make Eli Lilly stock a buy?

    Industry observers note that the potential label expansion for Zepbound in adolescents appears attractive, and it once again highlights Eli Lilly's strength in one of its core therapeutic areas. Eli Lilly is also running clinical trials for Zepbound in patients between six and 11 years of age, which could add more than five million patients to its addressable market, provided the medicine proves effective in this study.

    Sources indicate that and we haven't even mentioned the several other clinical trial candidates the company has in weight loss or, for that matter, the deep pipeline it has built in other therapeutic areas, such as oncology. So, Eli Lilly's prospects look attractive. The stock has outperformed broader equities this year -- and since the turn of the decade, for that matter -- but there may be plenty of upside left.

    • In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Recent findings suggest that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Recent findings suggest that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    With 64 years of consecutive dividend increases, Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) is one of the Dividend Kings, if not one of the quintessential blue chip dividend stocks. This dividend growth and dependability are likely major factors behind the stock's continued presence in Berkshire Hathaway's portfolio.

    Sources indicate that berkshire's 400 million-share position, worth around $39.6 billion, generates nearly $850 million in annual dividend income. Investors operating on a smaller scale could make it a core holding to build their own steady income stream.

    It has been revealed that coca-Cola currently pays a $0.53-per-share cash dividend, equating to $2.12 in annual dividends per share. To generate $1,000 per month, or $12,000 per year, divide $12,000 by $2.12. This gives you around 5,661 shares.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    With Coca-Cola recently trading at around $99 per share, you would need to invest $560,439 to generate $12,001.32 in annual dividend income. This works out to a dividend yield of around 2.15%. At a time when the federal funds rate stands at nearly 3.9%, this may not sound significant, but consider the other benefits of buying and holding Coca-Cola over the long term.

    Industry observers note that over the past decade, dividend increases have averaged 4.45% annually. If this trend continues and Coca-Cola keeps raising its dividend by 4% to 5% per year, a decade from now, this same position could be generating between $1,480 and $1,628 per month in dividend income.

    According to recent reports, although Coca-Cola has trailed the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) in total returns over the last decade, the stock has outperformed the market index in more recent years, particularly over the past year. That's not to say that this trend will continue. After this recent hot streak, for instance, Coca-Cola shares have reached a relatively high valuation of 28.5 times forward earnings. While it may be a stronger buy on a pullback, its dividend durability and growth still make it a solid core position in a long-term income-focused portfolio.
